title: introduce-tenant-privacy-profiles-kms-wrap-shim-and-rbac-migration-path
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds per-tenant privacy profiles (opt-in), KMS wrap helper for deterministic pseudonymization, a dry-run RBACv1->v2 shim, operator docs, and tests. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind `privacy_profiles` flag.
body:
Summary: Add a tenant-level 'privacy profile' feature that lets customers opt tenants into a constrained audit footprint. This PR implements: 1) a small, opt-in transport shim that applies deterministic pseudonymization to configured audit fields before logs leave the control plane, using envelope KMS wrapping for provenance; 2) a KMS wrap helper to derive per-tenant wrapping keys (no new persistent keys — uses existing CMKs with derived encryption context); 3) an RBAC migration shim that allows operators to run RBACv1->v2 evaluation in dry-run mode and produce a compatibility report; and 4) operator docs, e2e tests, and CI checks.
Motivation: customers in regulated industries requested a way to limit personally identifiable fields in audit streams while preserving provable integrity and KMS-backed provenance for forensics. Previous approaches either stripped too much context (lossy redaction) or required full service-side key management. This approach balances audit usefulness and privacy by pseudonymizing identifiable fields deterministically and signing the wrapped envelope with existing CMKs so auditors can prove authenticity without revealing raw values.
Compatibility and safety: feature is opt-in per tenant via tenant config; no default behavior change. The RBAC migration shim runs in passive mode unless explicitly enabled and emits decision diffs only to the operator audit bucket.
Checklist:
- [x] Design doc: ENG-4211 (linked)
- [x] KMS wrap helper implementation
- [x] Audit pseudonymizer middleware
- [x] RBACv2 compatibility shim + reporter
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] End-to-end test against redwood-private-installer local cluster
- [x] Operator docs and runbook
- [x] Feature flag gating
Implementation notes:
- Added audit/pseudonymizer middleware which takes a tenant privacy profile (list of paths to pseudonymize) and replaces values with HMAC-based pseudonyms. The HMAC key is derived via KMS GenerateDataKey with a tenant-specific encryption context; the raw HMAC key is never persisted.
- Implemented kms/wrap helper that performs a single AES-GCM envelope wrap where the wrapping key material is derived from an AWS/Cloud KMS CMK and the tenant id+profile tag as the encryption context. The resulting envelope contains a provenance header with CMK ARN and encryption context fingerprint.
- RBAC shim: new rbac/migration/dryrun service that, given a tenant and a set of requests, evaluates against RBACv1 and RBACv2 paths and emits a compact diff. Reports are JSON-lines stored to the operator-only S3 bucket by default.
- Telemetry: added metric privacy.profile.applied{tenant} and privacy.profile.pseudonymize_latency_seconds.
- Security: HMAC derivation uses KDF with KMS-provided key material and HKDF-SHA256, nonce per pseudonymization call, and the pseudonym is base64url of first 16 bytes; raw values removed from the emitted audit line.
- Rollout plan: feature flag privacy_profiles toggles middleware; start with canary tenants, roll to 10% via console, then full rollout.
- Mitigations: we keep a reversible provenance envelope (wrapped key + CMK reference) for forensic reconstruction in emergencies but require an elevated operator workflow with approvals and audit gating (SUP-3248).

Testing notes:
- Initial CI run hit a flake in the e2e harness (timeout waiting for local cluster), test fixed in fa9013b with retry/backoff logic.
- Added an integration matrix covering AWS and GCP KMS providers in CI to validate encryption-context usage.
- Manual runs against a demo tenant confirmed pseudonymization is deterministic and provable using the envelope provenance.
Review conversation (selected):
- Marcus Holt (reviewer): "This is an important feature for compliance customers. Two concerns: 1) risk of exposing KMS ARNs in audit output; 2) potential performance impact on high-throughput tenants. Can we avoid leaking full ARNs and measure latency?"
- Asha (author): "We include a CMK fingerprint (sha256 truncated) rather than full ARN by default. I added metric privacy.profile.pseudonymize_latency_seconds and a note in the runbook about TTFB. Also added an optional config to redact CMK identifiers in operator-view reports."
- Tessa Nguyen (reviewer): "Please ensure the migration shim cannot be toggled by tenant-level admins; only operator roles should run it."
- Asha: "Agree — restricted via operator-only RBAC role; enforced in rbac/migration service and tested in unit tests."
- Ravi Kapoor (reviewer): "The reversible envelope for emergency reconstruction is sensitive — require two-operator approval and time-limited access."
- Asha: "Added a runbook section requiring two operator approvals and a signed ticket (SUP-3248). Envelope unwrapping writes to an operator-only audit channel and is logged with the approval reference."
Follow-ups and fixes:
- fa9013b: add retry/backoff to e2e harness (addressed flake).
- e2b4d66: tighten logging to avoid recording raw fields on errors (security review request).
CI and checks summary:
- unit tests: pass
- integration (local): pass after rerun
- lint: pass
- static-analysis (gosec/dep): pass with a single LOW finding (documented)
- e2e-privacy-profile job: pass on second run
Merge: squashed and merged via "Squash and merge" on 2026-03-06.
Post-merge tasks:
- [x] Publish operator docs to internal KB
- [x] Add privacy_profiles flag to console feature flags list
- [x] Schedule canary rollout for 2026-03-10
- [x] Add follow-up ticket to re-evaluate CMK fingerprinting strategy (ENG-4280)
Known limitations and notes:
- Pseudonymization reduces but does not guarantee irreversibility if attacker gains CMK access; rely on CMK protections and operator approval gating.
- Migration shim focuses on decision parity; complex policy constructs may need manual review.
- Performance overhead: measured median pseudonymize latency 4.8ms on a canary tenant; batching will be considered in a follow-up if customers require sub-ms SLOs.
Contributing docs and operator runbook included in docs/ops. If there's concern about the provable envelope, please reach out to the security group (SEC-88) for threat modeling.
